jāṇussoṇisutta:
[Jāṇussoṇi+sutta]  CL=7 In response to the Brahmin Jāṇussoṇi"s question, the Buddha explained:
The view that 'everything exists' represents one extreme (inferior dhamma), and the view that 'nothing exists' represents another extreme (inferior dhamma). The Buddha does not approach these two extremes but follows the Middle Path. From ignorance (avijjā) arises volitional formations (saṅkhāra); from volitional formations arises consciousness (viññāṇa); and so on, illustrating the cycle of saṃsāra. Conversely, with the cessation of ignorance (avijjā), volitional formations cease; with the cessation of volitional formations, consciousness ceases, and so on, leading to the cessation or breaking of the saṃsāric cycle.
